# The folder parts

Every part that lives in its own folder, with its sample. The Format page shows each as source, drawing and LLM view.

## Audio

An audio part is a player of our own. The wave is drawn from a small peaks file and moves with the sound; chapters split it, a marker flags one moment, and the transcript follows the voice.

```audio src="media/talk.mp3" title="A page that talks" duration=0:57 wave=bars skip=10 transcript=open
peaks: media/talk.peaks.json
chapter 0:00 Welcome
chapter 0:24 The transcript
chapter 0:38 The marker
marker 0:38 Where the example crashed [bad]
0:00 Ana: Welcome back. Today we look at a page that can talk.
0:04 Ben: A page that talks. Do you mean the audio part?
0:08 Ana: Yes. You write one fence, with a file, a title, and a few lines of transcript.
0:14 Ben: And the reader sees a wave that moves while the voice plays.
0:18 Ana: The wave is drawn from a small peaks file, so it appears before the sound starts.
0:24 Ben: What about people who cannot listen right now?
0:27 Ana: The transcript follows the voice. Tap a line, and the player jumps there.
0:33 Ben: Chapters split the wave into parts, and a marker flags one moment.
0:38 Ana: Here is the marker. This is where the example crashed.
0:42 Ben: And a language model reads the same page as plain text.
0:46 Ana: It gets the title, the chapters, and the transcript, never a picture of a wave.
0:52 Ben: That is the whole part. Press play, and listen again.
```

`wave=mirror` reflects the wave, `wave=dots` draws it in dots, `wave=live` shows a window of the sound that scrolls past "now", and `compact` makes one row. The colour is a word (`tone=c4`), never a hex value.

```audio src="media/talk.mp3" title="Mirror wave, in family colour 4" wave=mirror tone=c4 height=s duration=0:57
peaks: media/talk.peaks.json
```

```audio src="media/talk.mp3" title="Compact" compact wave=line duration=0:57
peaks: media/talk.peaks.json
```

## Calendar

The host supplies no clock here: Today returns to the authored date. Explore the views, switch calendars and open events. A narrow part starts with three days.

```calendar title="Release week" tz=Europe/London date=2026-11-23 view=week hours=08-18
calendar team "Team" [c2]
2026-11-23 09:00-09:20 Stand-up in team every weekday times=5
2026-11-24 10:00-11:30 Design review @ Studio in team note="Bring the mock-ups"
2026-11-24 10:30-11:00 Review notes in team
2026-11-25 all day Code freeze [warn]
2026-11-26 18:00-19:00 Sydney call tz=Australia/Sydney
```

The static form keeps a complete dated list without controls.

```calendar title="Release checklist" tz=Europe/London date=2026-11-23 static
calendar team "Team" [c2]
2026-11-23 09:00-09:20 Stand-up in team every weekday times=3
2026-11-25 all day Code freeze [warn]
```

## Chart kinds

Eight more kinds of a `chart`, each a YAML map with `kind:` at the top: raw values are counted, quartiled or smoothed when the page is built, so a model reads the table. Hover, tap or focus a bin, box, stage, block or day for its card; the arrow keys walk the data.

```chart
kind: histogram
title: How long a request takes
x: { label: latency, format: duration-ms }
y: { label: requests }
bins: 12
```

## Compare

**A comparison matrix puts options side by side, one line for each thing you judge them on.** The first line names the options; every other line is a criterion and one value for each option, in the same order. A note in round brackets shows when a reader hovers, focuses or taps the value. With `winner=on` the best value of each yes/no, scored or good/bad row is marked; `pick=` flags the option you recommend.

```compare title="Which queue?" winner=on pick=Kafka
options: Redis Streams [c1], Kafka [c2], SQS [c3]
Ordering: yes, yes, partial (FIFO queues only)
Runs itself: no, no, yes
Throughput: 3, 5, 3 (score 1-5)
Latency (lower is better): 4 ms (in one region), 12 ms, 25 ms
Replay old messages: yes (until trimmed), yes (by offset), no
Cost at our size: good, bad, good (pay per request)
Team knows it: yes, partial (two people), yes
```

With `view=single`, a phone shows one option at a time, chosen from buttons. Here the values are plain words and good, warn and bad, so no row is marked as the best.

```compare title="Where to host the docs" view=single
options: Own servers, Static host, Wiki service
Set-up time: a week, an hour, a day
Custom domain: good, good, warn (paid plan only)
Search: warn (add one), warn (add one), good
Who can edit: developers, developers, anyone with an account
```

## Compare image

**A before-and-after picture lays two images of the same size on top of each other, with a bar between them.** Drag the bar (or anywhere on the picture), press the arrow keys, or tap the picture to flip from one to the other; the two labels jump to a whole image. Each image line gives the address and the alt text in quotes, which is what a screen reader and an LLM read. The address goes through the host's URL policy (a relative path, http or https; never `data:`). The two sample images are the files `before-light.svg` and `after-dark.svg` in this part's `media/` folder: a host serves that folder as `media/`.

```compare-image title="A dashboard, light and dark" before="Light" after="Dark"
before: media/before-light.svg "A dashboard with four tiles and a bar chart on a light page"
after: media/after-dark.svg "The same dashboard on a dark page"
```

## Diff

A `diff` block holds what `git diff` prints. It is drawn as a diff view: a file header with how much changed, line numbers on both sides, the changed words marked inside a changed line, and long unchanged runs folded. It is split on a wide part and unified on a narrow one; the buttons switch it, and `view=split` or `view=unified` fixes it. On a phone the lines do not wrap: the numbers and the sign stay in view while the code scrolls inside its box.

```diff
diff --git a/src/server.ts b/src/server.ts
index 4b825dc..9f3c1a7 100644
--- a/src/server.ts
+++ b/src/server.ts
@@ -12,9 +12,10 @@ export function start(config: Config) {
   const port = config.port ?? 8080;
-  const host = "localhost";
+  const host = config.host ?? "0.0.0.0";
   const server = createServer(handler);
-  server.listen(port, host);
+  server.listen(port, host, () => log.info("listening", { port, host }));
   register(server);
   watch(config);
   return server;
@@ -48,6 +49,6 @@ export function stop(server: Server) {
   unwatch();
-  server.close();
+  server.close(() => log.info("closed"));
 }
@@ -80,18 +81,19 @@ export function reload(server: Server) {
   const next = readConfig();
-  if (next.port !== current.port) restart(server);
+  if (next.port !== current.port || next.host !== current.host) restart(server);
   current = next;
   emit("reload", next);
   mark("reload");
   audit(next);
   notify(next);
   flush();
   settle();
   prune();
   index();
   compact();
   verify();
+  log.debug("reloaded", { port: next.port });
   return server;
 }
```

With `static` the diff is drawn whole, with no button: every file open, and a folded run only says how many lines it holds.

```diff static
--- a/src/greet.ts
+++ b/src/greet.ts
@@ -1,4 +1,4 @@
 export function greet(name: string) {
-  return "Hello, " + name;
+  return `Hello, ${name}!`;
 }
```

## Downloads

A card for each file: a type icon, its size, a plain download link, and a checksum that copies on a tap, with the line that checks it. Nothing is counted and nothing is fetched until the reader presses Download.

```downloads title="Files for this page"
media/report.pdf "The report, first pages" 209 KB sha256=d14bdfa9e9a37c960e8a2835fd6c0e75aa6e201e1e967d18159378e3de124372
media/talk.mp3 "The spoken sample" 229 KB sha256=8ed40d5dc963c74c457b987f9af4b4f3a33f1c13aa7a547cd3e959bf6fcd5d55
media/build.json "The hand-written animation" 6.4 KB note="A Lottie file with no expressions and no images."
https://example.com/durian-markdown-0.7.0.tar.gz "Source archive (an example address)" 1.2 MB sha256=2c26b46b68ffc68ff99b453c1d30413413422d706483bfa0f98a5e886266e7ae note="The address is an example; nothing is fetched until you press Download."
media/requests.csv "Raw data" 15.4 KB note="One row per request."
```

## Explore

A fence in the data's own language, followed by `explore`, becomes a foldable tree with a search box, a copy-path button on every key and a **jq subset** query box. It reads JSON, YAML or CSV (a CSV's rows become objects). `query=` is the starting query. The box runs our own small jq (the "jq subset": paths, pipes, `select`, `map`, `keys`, `length`, `sort_by`, `group_by`, `to_entries`, `test`, string interpolation, building objects and arrays); a query that needs more work than a page may use says so, and a function outside the subset is named, never answered wrongly. It lacks assignment (`|=`), `reduce`, `foreach`, `def`, `paths`, `del`, `sub`, `gsub`, `match` and `walk`.

```json explore title="One order" query=".lines[] | select(.qty > 1)"
{
  "id": "o-7",
  "customer": { "id": "c-12", "name": "Ana", "tags": ["vip", "early"] },
  "lines": [
    { "sku": "tea", "qty": 2, "price": 3.5 },
    { "sku": "cup", "qty": 1, "price": 8 },
    { "sku": "pot", "qty": 3, "price": 12.25 }
  ],
  "paid": true,
  "note": null
}
```

The same reader takes YAML and CSV. TOML exploration is refused until a TOML reader is available; the TOML example below is ordinary code:

```yaml explore title="A service config" query=".limits | map_values(ascii_upcase)"
service: shop
replicas: 3
limits:
  cpu: 500m
  mem: 256Mi
hosts:
  - name: app-1.example.com
    zone: a
  - name: app-2.example.com
    zone: b
```

```toml
[server]
host = "198.51.100.7"
port = 8443
tls = true

[limits]
cpu = "500m"
```

```csv explore title="Latency by region" query="sort_by(.p95) | reverse | .[0].region"
region,p50,p95,requests
us-west,42,120,1200000
eu-central,55,180,830000
ap-south,70,260,410000
```

## Fishbone

Causes by category along a spine into the effect. In a narrow column the spine turns vertical.

```fishbone title="Why is checkout slow?"
effect: Checkout takes 4 seconds at p95
People: on-call is new to the service
Process: no load test before a release
  only staging has real data
Tools: the ORM loads every line item
  one query per line
Environment: the database is in another region
```

With steps, the bones come in one at a time, and `highlight` lights one.

```fishbone title="Why did the deploy fail?"
effect: The deploy rolled back
@step The first two causes.
Config: a key was renamed in one place only
Tests: the contract test was skipped
@step The third, and the one to fix first.
Release: two services shipped in the wrong order
highlight Config
```

## Flame chart and flame graph

A traced request and folded profiler stacks. Tap a frame to zoom; search highlights matching frames.

```flame title="One request, traced" unit=ms

  2 14 auth.check
  15 95 handler.order
    16 70 db.query
    72 90 render.page
  96 118 respond.write
```

```flame title="CPU, 30 seconds" unit=samples colour=heat
main;serve;handle;parse 120
main;serve;handle;db.query 300
main;serve;handle;db.query;lock.wait 80
main;serve;handle;render.page 95
main;serve;gc 45
main;serve;accept 30
main;housekeeping;flush 60
```

## Gantt

A task line is `<id> "label" <start> <end or length> [progress%] [done] [colour]`; a start is a date or `after <id> ...`; `milestone` is a point; `section` groups the lines after it. `today=` draws a line (never the real clock). Hover, tap or focus a bar for its dates and what it waits for; Day, Week and Month change the scale.

```gantt title="Release 2.0" today=2026-12-09
section Build
design "Design" 2026-12-01 .. 2026-12-04 done
api "API" after design 8d 60%
ui "Screens" after design 6d
section Ship
beta "Beta" after api ui 3d [warn]
launch "Launch" milestone after beta
```

Under steps, `progress`, `done` and `move` change the plan as time passes; a slip carries the tasks after it. `workdays=on` makes lengths skip Saturday and Sunday, and `critical=on` outlines the longest chain.

```gantt title="A release that slips" workdays=on critical=on today=2026-12-14
section Build
design "Design" 2026-12-01 .. 2026-12-04 done
api "API" after design 8d 40%
ui "Screens" after design 6d
section Test
qa "QA" after api ui 5d
@step The plan on 1 December
@step Design is done, the API is under way
progress api 60%
progress ui 100%
@step The API slips by a week
move api 2026-12-14
launch "Launch" milestone after qa
```

## Glossary

Terms defined once. Where a term is used in the text, its first use in each section is a button with a dotted underline: hover it, tap it, or focus it and press Enter to read the meaning.

```glossary title="Words we use"
term "UL" also "ubiquitous language": the words a team agrees on and uses in code and in talk
term bc "bounded context" also "context map": one part of the system with its own **words**; see [the book](https://example.com/ddd)
```

Each team keeps its own UL inside a bounded context. The second use of UL in the same section stays plain text: UL.

## Graph

A graph is for finding your way around a big network: what uses what, and what breaks if one part goes. Write `group` and `node` lines, then one edge a line (`a -> b`, with a label in quotes if it needs one). A node an edge names and no line declares is added (here the outside libraries). `layout=layers` puts each package above what it uses. **Explore it:** search a package, tap one to focus it and its neighbours (1 or 2 steps out), fold a group into one box, pan and zoom; the list beside the graph shows its links in and out. Its LLM view is the graph itself, as lines.

```graph title="A shop's packages, and what each one uses" layout=layers
group apps "apps" [c1]
group domain "domain" [c2]
group data "data access" [c6]
group core "core" [c3]
node web "web shop" in apps
node admin "admin console" in apps
node worker "background worker" in apps
node cart, checkout, catalog, accounts, orders, search in domain
node db "database" in data
node cache, queue in data
node config, log in core
web -> cart, checkout, search
admin -> catalog, accounts, orders
worker -> orders
cart -> cache, db
checkout -> db, queue
catalog -> db, cache
accounts -> db
orders -> db, queue
search -> cache
queue -> ioredis
cache -> ioredis, config
db -> pg, config, log
```

`layout=force` pulls linked services together and pushes the rest apart, so the clusters show. It fits calls between services, where there is no top or bottom. An id may carry a numbered range: `node db-orders-{1..6} in data` declares six shards, and `orders -> db-orders-{1..6}` draws a line to each. **Fold a group** (beside the graph, or a double tap on its box) and its lines join on one box with a count; **Fold groups** folds them all. A graph over 300 nodes, or one that would be drawn too small to touch in its box (a phone), starts with every group folded. Its LLM view is the nodes by group, the edges as `a -> b` lines, and the most connected nodes: here far over 400 tokens, so a `:::llm` says it in short.

```graph title="Calls between the services of a shop" layout=force size=l
group edge "edge" [c1]
group identity "identity" [c2]
group catalog "catalog" [c3]
group orders "orders" [c4]
group payments "payments" [c5]
group fulfil "fulfilment" [c6]

node auth, sessions, users, profiles, roles, mfa, sso, tokens, consent, audit, password-reset, email-verify, devices, risk-score, api-keys in identity
node catalog-api, products, variants, inventory, prices, promos, reviews, search-api, indexer, recs, media, categories, brands, bundles, wishlist in catalog
node cart-api, checkout, orders-api, order-events, invoices, returns, refunds, tax, shipping-quote, gift-cards, loyalty, quotes, subscriptions, order-history, fraud in orders

psp-a, psp-b -> pay-events
wallets -> ledger
payouts -> ledger, psp-a, settlements
ledger -> fx, dw
disputes -> chargebacks, psp-a, psp-b
settlements -> ledger, dw
pay-events -> event-bus
chargebacks -> ledger
billing -> pay-api, receipts
receipts -> email, blob-store
fulfil-api -> warehouses, dispatch, labels, tracking
warehouses -> stock-sync, picking
picking -> packing
packing -> labels
labels -> carriers, blob-store
carriers -> tracking
tracking -> notify, event-bus
dispatch -> couriers, slots, carriers
stock-sync -> inventory, event-bus
returns-in -> warehouses, refunds
notify -> sms, email
event-bus -> fulfil-api, indexer, notify, dw, audit
scheduler -> jobs
jobs -> backups, indexer, payouts, settlements
alerts -> metrics, logs
mesh -> dns, traces, metrics
backups -> blob-store
ci -> registry
config-svc -> flags, secrets
secrets -> kms
gateway, auth, checkout, pay-api, orders-api -> mesh
```

:::llm
A force-laid call graph of a shop: 120 services in 8 groups, 232 calls. Edge (cdn, waf, gateway, three backends for web, mobile and admin, graphql, ws-hub ...) calls identity (auth, sessions, users, tokens, mfa, sso ...) and catalog (catalog-api, products, prices, search-api, recs ...). Checkout calls cart-api, tax, shipping-quote, fraud, loyalty, pay-api and orders-api; orders-api writes six shards, db-orders-1 to db-orders-6. pay-api calls card-vault, two payment providers, wallets, three-ds and the ledger. Events go through event-bus to fulfilment (warehouses, picking, packing, labels, carriers, tracking), the indexer, notify, the warehouse (dw) and audit. Platform: config, flags, secrets, kms, metrics, logs, traces, the mesh, scheduler and jobs. Most connected: orders-api (5 in, 9 out), auth, catalog-api, pay-api, event-bus (6 in, 5 out).
:::

`layout=radial centre=<node>` puts one node in the middle and each ring one step further away, in either direction: what it uses and what uses it. Use it to answer "what touches this?". A small graph needs no `:::llm`: its LLM view is the graph itself, as lines.

```graph title="What touches the sign-in service" layout=radial centre=auth
group callers "calls sign-in" [c1]
group needs "sign-in calls" [c6]
node web, mobile, admin, cli in callers
node sessions, users, mfa, tokens in needs
node auth "sign-in"
web, mobile, admin, cli -> auth
auth -> sessions, users, mfa, tokens
mfa -> sms "codes"
tokens -> kms "signing keys"
sessions, users -> postgres
```

`static` draws the part still: the groups with how many nodes each holds, and a line that counts the edges between two groups. It is for print, a PDF, an email, or a reader who asks for less motion.

```graph title="The same sign-in graph, drawn still" layout=radial centre=auth static
group callers "calls sign-in" [c1]
group needs "sign-in calls" [c6]
node web, mobile, admin, cli in callers
node sessions, users, mfa, tokens in needs
node auth "sign-in"
web, mobile, admin, cli -> auth
auth -> sessions, users, mfa, tokens
mfa -> sms "codes"
tokens -> kms "signing keys"
sessions, users -> postgres
```

## Http

An `http` block is a request and, after a blank line, its response, as text. It is drawn as a method tag and the address (the query split into names and values), the headers (folded after six), the body (JSON is pretty and can be folded), the status as a tag coloured by its class, and a button that copies the request as `curl`. A secret in a header is never written out: use a placeholder such as `<token>`.

```http title="Create an order"
POST /v1/orders?dry_run=false&currency=usd HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Idempotency-Key: 6f1c2d0e
User-Agent: shop-cli/2.4
X-Request-Id: req-7a91

{ "sku": "tea", "qty": 2, "ship": { "to": "198.51.100.7", "express": true }, "notes": ["gift", "no receipt"] }

HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Content-Type: application/json
Location: /v1/orders/o-7

{ "id": "o-7", "status": "open", "total": { "amount": 1840, "currency": "usd" } }
```

With `static` the whole message is drawn: every header, the whole JSON tree, no button.

```http static
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: application/json
Cache-Control: no-store

{ "error": "not_found", "detail": { "resource": "order", "id": "o-9" } }
```

## Log

A fence named `log`. It reads JSON lines, logfmt and the common "time level message key=value" shape. The filter box speaks **LogQL** (Grafana Loki's query language): `{level="error"}`, `|= "timeout"`, `!= "health"`, `|~ "5\\d\\d"`, `| status >= 500`; a box that starts with neither `{` nor `|` is plain words. Only the query half of LogQL is read, never metric queries. `filter=` is the starting filter. The author (often an agent) points at what matters with `@highlight` lines: a LogQL filter or `line 3-5`, a colour word and the reason in quotes.

```log title="The failed deploy" labels="app=shop, env=prod" filter="{level=~\"warn|error\"}"
2026-11-20T10:08:01Z info  deploy started version=1.4
2026-11-20T10:08:12Z info  migration applied name=0042
2026-11-20T10:09:03Z warn  cache miss rate high rate=0.41
2026-11-20T10:09:05Z error request failed path=/cart status=500 err="timeout after 30s" span=checkout trace=request
2026-11-20T10:09:06Z error request failed path=/cart status=500 err="timeout after 30s" span=checkout trace=request
@highlight |= "timeout" [bad] "every failure is the same timeout"
@highlight line 3 [warn] "the first sign"
```

## Lottie

A Lottie file is a drawing that moves. This one was written by hand for the sample: a box fills with blocks, one row at a time, then a tick appears. It plays while it is on screen, stops off it, and shows one still frame when the reader asks for less motion. The `colours:` line maps names inside the file to theme colours, so it follows light and dark.

```lottie src="media/build.json" title="What happens while it builds" loop
alt: A box fills with blocks, one row at a time, then a tick appears.
colours: dh-c1 = c1, dh-c2 = c2, dh-c3 = c3, dh-good = good
```

## Map and routes

Places and written routes work without a tile provider. A dashed route has no road geometry; the host may supply its own router.

```map title="Walk to the garden"
place start "Library" 51.507, -0.128 [c1] note="Meet by the entrance"
place garden "Garden" 51.511, -0.117 [c2]
route walk "Morning walk" by=walk [c2]: start -> 51.508, -0.123 -> garden
@step Meet at the library.
focus start
@step Follow the written route.
show walk
focus walk
```

Country values and flows share one map and one value list; the map is framed on the places that have a value.

```map title="Daily flow" unit="units per day" scale=steps steps=4
fill DE 83.2
fill FR 68.4
arc DE -> FR 24 "Daily flow" [c2]
```

US states work the same way.

```map title="Western states" unit="units per day" scale=steps steps=4
fill US-CA 39.5
fill US-WA 7.7
fill US-AZ 7.2
fill US-OR 4.2
fill US-NV 3.1
```

The globe uses the same data; with no WebGL it falls back to the flat map.

```map title="Global flow" view=globe spin=off unit="units per day"
fill DE 83.2
fill FR 68.4
arc DE -> FR 24 "Daily flow" [c2]
```

A static globe is a flat map with all its values, ready to print.

```map title="A still map" view=globe static
fill DE 83.2
fill FR 68.4
```

## Maths (`$...$`, `$$...$$` and `math`)

The area of a circle is $A = \pi r^2$, and a sum of the first $n$ numbers is:

$$
\sum_{k=1}^{n} k = \frac{n(n+1)}{2}
$$

The same in a `math` block, with a fraction, a root and a matrix:

```math
x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} \qquad
\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}
```

Prices stay text: it costs $5 and $10, and `$not maths$` in code is left alone.

## PDF

pdf.js draws the pages on a canvas, and its text layer makes the words selectable and searchable. The file below was printed from a small made-up document. The viewer works a page at a time; try the search box, the outline and the zoom.

```pdf src="media/sample.pdf" title="A sample document" page=1 height=l
```

`view=scroll` lays every page out in one scrolling column and draws the ones near the window.

```pdf src="media/sample.pdf" title="The same file, scrolling" view=scroll height=s
```

## Citations (`[@key]` and `references`)

A mark in the text opens its entry: marks make a study easier to read [@smith2020, p. 12], and two together are one group [@smith2020; @lee2019]. Hover, focus or tap a mark for the entry.

```references style=apa title="References"
- id: smith2020
  author: Smith, Jane; Lee, Kim
  title: A study of marks
  in: Journal of Studies
  year: 2020
  volume: 12
  issue: 3
  pages: 10-20
  doi: 10.1234/jbs.2020.4
- id: lee2019
  author: Lee, Kim
  title: Notes on lists
  type: web
  publisher: Example Press
  year: 2019
  url: https://example.com/notes
  accessed: 2026-11-20
```

## Sankey

A flow a line, `from -> to: amount`; `node <id> "label" [colour]` only to name or colour one. Hover, tap or focus a band to light its path and read its share.

```sankey title="Where a request's time goes" unit=ms
request -> auth: 12
request -> handler: 80
handler -> db: 55
handler -> render: 20
handler -> cache: 5
node db "Postgres" [c3]
node cache "Redis" [c2]
```

Flows under a step appear in it: the bands grow out of their source. In a narrow column, a sankey with more than three columns runs top to bottom.

```sankey title="Where the month's budget goes" unit=USD
income -> payroll: 62000
income -> infra: 21000
income -> tools: 6000
income -> reserve: 11000
@step The money in and where it goes
@step Infrastructure breaks down
infra -> compute: 12500
infra -> storage: 5200
infra -> network: 3300
@step Compute splits by team
compute -> web: 7000
compute -> data: 4100
compute -> ml: 1400
node income "Revenue" [c1]
node payroll "People" [c4]
node infra "Infrastructure" [c6]
```

## Sequence

Who calls whom, in order. A call is a solid arrow, a reply a dashed one; a block (`loop`, `alt`, `opt`, `par`) frames the messages inside it. An LLM reads the messages as a numbered list.

```sequence title="One init call"
actor dev "developer"
participant cli "CLI"
participant tc "template container"
dev -> cli: scaffold create
cli -> tc: init call, all answers
tc --> cli: question reply
note tc: the script stopped at a question
loop until no question is left
  cli -> tc: init call, one more answer
  tc --> cli: question reply
end
cli --> dev: project written
```

With `@step` lines the story builds up one call a step: the earlier calls fade and the new one draws itself.

```sequence
participant cli "CLI"
participant tc "template container"
@step The CLI sends an init call with every answer it holds.
cli -> tc: init call: all answers
@step The script stops at a question and sends it back.
tc --> cli: question reply
@step The next init call carries one answer more.
cli -> tc: init call: one more answer
```

## Sparkline in a sentence (`:spark[...]`)

`:spark[3,5,2,8,9]` draws a tiny line the height of the text. Add `bar` for bars and a colour word for the colour: `:spark[3,5,2,8,9 bar good]`. Hover, tap or focus it to see the numbers. A model reads `(3, 5, 2, 8, 9)`.

Sign-ups this week were :spark[120,135,128,160,182,171,205] and rising, errors fell to :spark[14,12,15,9,7,4,3 bar good], and the queue is :spark[5,4,6,22,31,18,9 warn] after Wednesday's spike.

## Stacktrace

A fence named `stacktrace`. It reads a trace as printed by Go, .NET, Bun or Node, Dart, Java or Python: the error line, each cause in its own block, threads as groups. Library frames fold into one bar; frames of your own code (`app=`) are marked, and with `repo=` and `strip=` they name the file and line at the page’s pinned commit (when its front matter has a matching pins entry). Tap a frame to open it.

```stacktrace lang=go app=example.com/shop repo=example.com/shop strip=/src/shop/ title="A Go panic"
panic: runtime error: index out of range [3] with length 3

goroutine 18 [running]:
example.com/shop/cart.(*Cart).Item(...)
	/src/shop/cart/cart.go:42
example.com/shop/api.(*Server).getItem(0xc0001a2000, {0x7f1c, 0xc000124000}, 0xc000188000)
	/src/shop/api/items.go:88 +0x1d4
net/http.HandlerFunc.ServeHTTP(0xc000010040, {0x7f1c, 0xc000124000}, 0xc000188000)
	/usr/local/go/src/net/http/server.go:2136 +0x29
net/http.serverHandler.ServeHTTP({0xc00011e000}, {0x7f1c, 0xc000124000}, 0xc000188000)
	/usr/local/go/src/net/http/server.go:2938 +0x8e
```

## Stats

**Stat tiles are the row of big numbers at the top of a dashboard:** each tile is one figure with its name, how it changed and, if given, a tiny line of its recent values, so a reader takes in the state of something at a glance before reading on. The colour word in brackets says whether the change is good or bad (a fall in latency is good); it is never guessed from the sign.

```stats title="The week"
Requests "1.2 M" change=+12% [good] note="last 7 days" spark=3 5 4 6 8 9
p95 latency "180 ms" change=-8% [good] spark=9 8 8 7 7 6 5
Errors "0.4%" change=+0.1 [bad] note="of requests" spark=2 2 3 2 4 5
Cost "USD 412" change=+3% spark=4 4 5 5 5 6
```

A tile can also carry a glyph, a trend word and a sub-line. This block is `static`: it draws the tiles whole, the same in print.

```stats title="Garden at a glance" static
Yield "251 kg" glyph="✦" trend=up sub="Across three plots" change=+8% [good] note="this season" spark=180 192 205 224 251
Water "120 L" glyph="◉" trend=down sub="Stored rainwater" change=-6% [good] note="this week" spark=150 145 138 126 120
Beds "30" glyph="▦" trend=flat sub="Ready for planting" [c3]
```

## Timeline

One line per event, oldest first; an indented line is a detail. A year, a month or a day.

```timeline title="A release plan"
2026-05-04 Design review [c1]
  Scope and owners agreed
2026-09 First release [c2]
2026-11-21 Old drawing code removed [c5]
  New drawn parts take their place
2026-11-23 Version 2 ships [good] note="the big one"
```

With `dir=across` a wide screen lays it out sideways; a phone is always top to bottom. With steps, the events come in one group at a time.

```timeline title="A build-up" dir=across
2026 The idea
@step The first half of the year.
2026-03 A prototype
2026-06 A first user
@step The second half.
2026-09 First release [c2]
2026-12 Version 2 [good]
```

## Trace waterfall

A request across services. Fold spans, search, zoom the mini map, or switch to Flame.

```trace title="POST /checkout" unit=ms trace=t-7f3a
web        POST /checkout        0 842  user=u7 region=us-west-2
  gateway  route /checkout       3 838  route=checkout
    auth   verify.token          6  44  method=jwt
      db   SELECT sessions      10  38  rows=1
    cart   cart.load            47 205  items=3
      db   SELECT cart_items    52 121  rows=3
      db   SELECT prices       126 198  rows=3 cache=miss
    inventory stock.reserve     50 171  warehouse=w2
      db   UPDATE stock         57 166  rows=1 id=stock-update
    payment charge.card        208 812  provider=examplepay error="payment provider timed out"
      payment tls.connect      212 255
      payment provider.call    258 804  attempt=1 id=provider error="upstream timeout after 540 ms"
    queue  publish.retry       814 834  topic=payments.retry id=retry
@log db 130 warn "row lock held 94 ms" span=stock-update
@log payment 258 info "calling examplepay /v2/charge"
@log payment 804 error "upstream timeout after 540 ms, giving up"
@log queue 820 info "queued a retry for order o-2291"
@log web 840 error "answered 504 to the client"
@service db [c5] "Postgres"
```

:::llm
One checkout request, 842 ms, across 8 services. The payment provider call (258–804 ms) timed out, so charge.card and the request failed with a 504, and a retry was queued. Stock was reserved in parallel with the cart load and is not on the critical path; UPDATE stock in db waited 94 ms on a row lock.
:::

```trace title="GET /health" unit=ms open=2
web   GET /health        0 9
  api health.check       1 8
    db SELECT 1          2 6
```

```trace title="A flat list" unit=ms critical=off
web   GET /orders     0 60   id=a
api   orders.list     3 55   id=b parent=a
db    SELECT orders   8 40   id=c parent=b rows=25
api   orders.render  41 54   id=d parent=b
```

## Venn

Two to four sets in fixed, even shapes. It is not drawn to scale on purpose: the names are written in the regions. Hover, tap or focus a region to read its items; on a narrow screen they are listed under the figure.

```venn title="Who writes what"
set go "Go" [c1]
set rust "Rust" [c2]
set zig "Zig" [c3]
go: Ana, Ben
go & rust: Cy
go & rust & zig: Dee (writes all three)
rust: Eve, Fay
zig: 4 people
```

With steps, one set comes in at a time, with its regions.

```venn title="Adding one set at a time"
set a "Readers" [c4]
set b "Writers" [c5]
set c "Reviewers" [c6]
@step Readers and writers overlap.
a: Ana, Ben
a & b: Cy
b: Dee
@step Reviewers join; some people do all three.
c: Eve
a & b & c: Fay
```

## Video

A video part keeps the browser's video and draws its own controls: a big play button on the poster, a bar with the chapters as segments (point at it to see the chapter and a still), captions drawn by us from a WebVTT file, picture in picture and full screen. The picture here is a made-up moving gradient.

```video src="media/sample.mp4" poster="media/poster.jpg" title="Colours drifting" duration=0:12
captions: media/sample.en.vtt "English" default
thumbs: media/thumbs.vtt
chapter 0:00 Warm
chapter 0:04 Cool
chapter 0:08 Bright
0:00 The colours drift slowly across the frame.
0:04 Captions are drawn by the part from a WebVTT file.
0:08 Press C to turn them off, and F for full screen.
```

`clip` is for a short screen recording that would otherwise be a GIF: it plays muted and in a loop while it is on screen, stops when it scrolls away, and stays still when the reader asks for less motion.

```video src="media/clip.mp4" title="A short silent loop" clip height=s
```

## Wardley map

Components by evolution (left to right) and visibility (top to bottom). Positions are named keys, so the two numbers cannot be swapped.

```wardley title="A tea shop"
anchor customer "Customer" visible=0.95 evolution=0.6
component cup "Cup of tea" visible=0.8 evolution=0.6
component tea "Tea" visible=0.6 evolution=0.8
component kettle "Kettle" visible=0.45 evolution=0.4
component power "Power" visible=0.1 evolution=0.85
customer -> cup
cup -> tea
cup -> kettle
kettle -> power
note "Kettles are a product now" visible=0.3 evolution=0.1
@step Today the kettle is a product we buy.
highlight kettle
@step A smart kettle moves it further to the right.
evolve kettle 0.65 "smart kettle"
```

## Weather

Example forecasts written in the source, not current conditions; nothing is fetched. The units menu on the part switches °C and °F, km/h, mph, m/s and knots, mm and inches, hPa and inHg, and your choice is remembered in this browser.

```weather place="San Francisco" unit=c tz=America/Los_Angeles
2026-11-22 sun 18/11 rain=0% wind=12km/h pressure=1021hPa
2026-11-23 partly 16/10 rain=10% wind=15km/h pressure=1018hPa
2026-11-24 rain 14/9 rain=80% wind=30km/h precip=6mm pressure=1004hPa
2026-11-25 storm 13/8 rain=95% wind=45km/h precip=14mm pressure=996hPa note="Ferry may stop"
2026-11-26 cloud 12/7 rain=30% wind=20km/h precip=1mm pressure=1009hPa
```

Hours work the same way, with one temperature, here written in °F and mph.

```weather place="Oakland" unit=f wind=mph tz=America/Los_Angeles
2026-11-24 06:00 fog 48 rain=5% wind=4mph
2026-11-24 09:00 cloud 52 rain=20% wind=8mph
2026-11-24 12:00 drizzle 57 rain=60% wind=11mph
2026-11-24 15:00 rain 59 rain=85% wind=14mph
2026-11-24 18:00 rain 55 rain=70% wind=12mph
2026-11-24 21:00 cloud 51 rain=25% wind=7mph
```

A different example forecast with `static`: drawn whole in the fence's unit, with no menu.

```weather static place="Sydney" title="Example spring forecast" unit=c wind=kmh
2026-11-22 sun 24/17 rain=0% wind=14km/h
2026-11-23 partly 22/16 rain=20% wind=18km/h
2026-11-24 rain 20/15 rain=70% wind=22km/h note="Showers later"
```
